In the [[mathematical]] field of [[potential theory]], '''Boggio's formula''' is an explicit formula for the [[Green's function]] for the polyharmonic [[Dirichlet problem]] on the ball of radius 1. It was discovered by the Italian mathematician [[Tommaso Boggio]]. 

The polyharmonic problem is to find a function ''u'' satisfying 
:<math>(-\Delta)^m u(x) = f(x)</math>
where ''m'' is a positive integer, and <math>(-\Delta)</math> represents the [[Laplace operator]]. The Green's function is a function satisfying
:<math>(-\Delta)^m G(x,y) = \delta(x-y)</math>
where <math>\delta</math> represents the [[Dirac delta function|Dirac delta distribution]], and in addition is equal to 0 up to order ''m-1'' at the boundary. 

Boggio found that the Green's function on the ball in ''n'' spatial dimensions is
:<math>G_{m,n} (x,y) = C_{m,n} |x-y|^{2m-n} \int_1^{\frac{\left||x|y - \frac{x}{|x|}\right|}{|x-y|}} (v^2-1)^{m-1} v^{1-n} dv</math>
The constant <math>C_{m,n}</math> is given by
:<math>C_{m,n} =\frac{1}{n e_n 4^{m-1} ((m-1)!)^2},</math> where <math>e_n = \frac{\pi^{\frac{n}{2}}}{\Gamma(1+\frac{n}{2})} </math>
